sections.body: Everything is made of tiny particles called ATOMS. An atom has a nucleus (protons and neutrons) with electrons around it.
An ELEMENT is a substance made of only one kind of atom, like oxygen (O), gold (Au) or carbon (C). The periodic table lists all 118 known elements.
A COMPOUND forms when atoms of two or more DIFFERENT elements are chemically bonded together. Water (H₂O) is 2 hydrogen atoms bonded to 1 oxygen atom.
A compound can be very different from its elements. Sodium is a reactive metal and chlorine is a poisonous gas, but together they make table salt (NaCl).
A MIXTURE is different: substances are mixed but not chemically bonded, like sand and water. You can often separate them by filtering.
Hydrogen is the most common element in the universe.

quiz.q: Which of these is an ELEMENT?
hints: An element has only one kind of atom.
Look at the chemical symbols. How many different letters (elements) does each have?
CO₂ has C and O, two elements, so it's a compound. Find the one with just one element.
quiz.explain: Oxygen is made of only one kind of atom, so it's an element. Water and salt are compounds.

options: It has two different elements chemically bonded
It is found in the ocean
hints: Think about the definition of a compound.
What do H and O stand for?
Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a compound because carbon and oxygen are bonded. Water is similar.
quiz.explain: Water is hydrogen and oxygen atoms chemically bonded together. That makes it a compound.

quiz.q: Sand stirred into water is a…
hints: Are the sand and water chemically bonded?
Can you separate them easily, for example by filtering?
Salad is lettuce and tomato mixed together. You can pick them apart. That's a…?
quiz.explain: Sand and water aren't bonded and can be separated by filtering, so it's a mixture.
